system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Seller Draft Review Against Buyer Playbook

**Scope:** This review is based only on the Seller's cover note, Seller Update summary and Disclosure Letter. I have not seen the underlying SPA mark-up or the data-room documents (DD-002 to DD-012), so I cannot confirm the clause text matches the summary. The Seller's cross-references (e.g., Clause 2/7, 3/6.3) are inconsistent, so the SPA draft should be checked against this summary.

**Preliminary point:** The Seller describes its positions as "FINAL", "settled at principal level", "market standard" and "the agreed commercial bargain." Under playbook sections 0.4 and 6.3, none of these labels binds us. We have no record of Amelia Frost giving authority for any of these positions. We should ask the Seller to identify any principal-level agreement in writing and treat the assertion as unverified until then.

---

## 1. Departures from Playbook (Summary Table)

| Topic | Seller position | Playbook position | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6m starting; 20% only with Amelia Frost written authority (none given) | Uses unauthorised fallback as opening position |
| De minimis (12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | 5x higher |
| Basket (12.2) | AUD 250,000, deductible (excess only) | AUD 50,000, first-dollar once exceeded | 5x higher and deductible rather than tipping |
| General claims period (12/13) | 18 months | 24 months (18 only with Amelia Frost approval; none given) | Unauthorised fallback |
| Fundamental/Title (12/13) | Same caps and time limits as general | Separate regime: 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar | Structural breach |
| Limitations/exclusive remedy/non-reliance (9.3, 12.8, 20.5) | Apply to "all Claims of any nature" | Fraud, wilful concealment, deliberate misconduct carved out of everything | No fraud carve-out |
| Disclosure (Sch. 7; DL 1.1, 1.2) | Whole data room, Accounts, public registers | Specific fair disclosure only | Prudent-search/deemed disclosure |
| Buyer knowledge (8.3) | Blanket exclusion, including "discoverable" matters and advisers' knowledge | Delete; any qualifier needs named persons and reasonable enquiry; never excuses title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities | Blanket exclusion |
| Bluefen (3/6.3) | Reasonable endeavours; consent "satisfied on delivery" | Effective consent and evidence of conditions before Completion; reasonable endeavours insufficient | Consent-on-delivery |
| Riverlark (2/7) | Release "following Completion" | Current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective releases; post-Completion release only with irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval | No payout at Completion |
| Bonuses (DL 5; funds flow) | Not itemised; "matter for the Seller" | Specific line item or seller-funded, including on-costs | Silently excluded |
| Ironquay IP (11.1) | SOW3 payment indemnity only; "adequate" | Broaden indemnity; preserve SOW3 cure | Too narrow |
| Export/privacy incident (4.6; Sch. 6) | "Not expected to be material" | Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; no assumption either way | Seller's characterisation is an assertion |
| Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k) | "Ordinary course" | Assess; no automatic Debt treatment or price deduction | Seller conclusion without evidence |
| Tax/IP (general regime) | "Settled" under general cap | Open; no unlimited liability assumed; no resolution | Premature closure |
| Title (DL 10) | DD-012 share register as proof of title | Independent evidence required; DD-012 is an internal source only | Not independent |

---

## 2. Material Issues and Reasoning

### A. Liability architecture (Issues 1 to 4 and 6)

**Cap (20% / AUD 4.8m).** The Seller has opened with our conditional fallback. The arithmetic is correct (20% × AUD 24m = AUD 4.8m), but the fallback can only be used with Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the draft, and none has been given. We should reject this and hold at 25% / AUD 6m. Any movement must be presented as a deal-team decision requiring her approval.

**Thresholds.** The AUD 250,000 basket is about 1% of price, which matches the Seller's "market" framing but not our playbook. The deductible structure is also materially worse for us: under the Seller's draft we absorb the first AUD 250,000 of general claims. Our position is AUD 5,000 de minimis and a AUD 50,000 first-dollar basket.

**Time limits.** 18 months is an unauthorised fallback; our position is 24 months. The Seller's proposal that "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims" is the more serious problem. It is a hidden general-regime override that would drag Title, Fundamental and fraud claims into the 18-month limit. The playbook prohibits this.

**Fundamental/Title.** The Seller proposes applying general caps and time limits to capacity and title warranties "for administrative simplicity." This is the most significant structural departure. Title and capacity are fundamental to what we are buying (100% of the shares), so they must sit in a separate regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, and outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. This should be a non-negotiable.

**Exclusive remedy and non-reliance (9.3, 12.8, 20.5).** These apply to "all Claims of any nature," with no fraud carve-out. That would leave a fraud claim capped, time-barred and subject to exclusive-remedy and non-reliance wording. The carve-out must apply to all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable, and cannot be waived. Counsel should confirm the enforceability of the carve-out under NSW law, but the position itself is not negotiable.

### B. Knowledge and disclosure (Issues 5 and 7)

**General disclosure (DL 1.1, 1.2).** Deeming the whole data room (including DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts and public registers as disclosed would hollow out every warranty. Each item would be disclosed by reference to a document we may never have read. Our playbook requires specific, fair disclosure. The DL 1.2 wording "without limiting any specific disclosure" makes this worse by stacking general disclosure on top of specific.

**Buyer knowledge (8.3).** The clause excludes claims for any matter the Buyer or its advisers "had knowledge" of, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records. This is effectively a prudent-buyer test and would catch matters we are only now uncovering in due diligence. Delete it. If the Seller insists on any qualifier, it must name specific Seller knowledge persons, require reasonable enquiry, and never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.

### C. Completion conditions and funds (Issues 8 to 10)

**Bluefen (approx. AUD 3.6m, about 30% of FY26 revenue).** This is a material customer consent. Reasonable endeavours is insufficient, and "treated as satisfied on delivery" means we could be obliged to complete before the consent is effective. DL §2 confirms no final written consent exists and conditions in clause 11.3 are not evidenced. Required position: effective consent plus evidence that the conditions are satisfied before Completion, as a condition precedent.

**Riverlark (approx. AUD 3.2m outstanding).** The Seller proposes a release "following Completion." DL §3 confirms the facility has not been repaid and no discharge is included. Required position: a current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion. A post-Completion release is only acceptable with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval. We should also confirm whether the price mechanics treat this debt as Debt under the debt-free/cash-free structure. The Seller's statement that the funds flow "reflects the agreed price mechanics" is unverified.

**Bonuses (DD-005, AUD 420,000).** The Seller says these are "a matter for the Seller" but does not itemise them in the funds flow. Under the playbook they must be either a specific line item or seller-funded, and the funds flow must not silently exclude them. On-costs (payroll tax, superannuation) are triggered by the bonuses but are not quantified in DL §5. Required: a specific line item or seller-funded arrangement, a quantified on-cost estimate, and confirmation of who pays what.

### D. Specific risk items (Issues 11 to 13)

**Ironquay IP (DL §4).** The indemnity covers only the SOW3 payment. DD-004 clause 7.3 makes transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials conditional on payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open, but this is not bank verification either way, and there is no receipt or confirmatory assignment. Required: broaden the indemnity to cover IP ownership and transfer defects, while preserving the SOW3 cure. Do not treat the AUD 180,000 as established.

**Export/privacy incident (DD-006; DL §6).** The Seller calls this "preliminary" and "not expected to be material." The disclosure does not establish whether unauthorised access occurred, the scope, or whether notification is required. The playbook requires us to assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction. Required: preservation of logs, a completed investigation, regular updates, and a specific indemnity or equivalent protection for pre-Completion incident exposure. The indemnity should be drafted without assuming any quantified loss, and the deal team should decide its scope.

**Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate, DL §8).** The Seller calls these ordinary-course costs. The disclosure does not say whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. Required: contracts, terms and timing, then assessment. There should be no automatic Debt classification or price deduction. The Seller's conclusion is not evidence.

### E. Open items (Issues 14 to 16)

**Tax and IP.** The Seller says these are "settled under the general regime." They are not. Under the playbook they remain open, with no unlimited liability and no resolution assumed. Tax and IP must stay separate from the general regime and must not be brought under it by a general override.

**Title (DL §10).** DD-012 is the Company's own share register, which is an internal source. The playbook requires independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence. Examples include an ASIC company extract, PPSR and encumbrance searches, board and shareholder approvals, and confirmation that there are no options or other rights over shares. The Seller's statement that DD-012 "evidences" title is not sufficient.

**Consents and third-party contracts (DL §§7, 9).** The office lease (landlord notification) and the Mossvale assignment restriction are not clearly characterised. The Seller's general "no consent legally required" statement (DL 1.4) is an assertion. We should require legal confirmation from the lease and Mossvale contract text, and confirm whether any change-of-control or notice obligation applies. The playbook does not set a fixed position here, so these are open diligence items.

---

## 3. Recommendations

**Must-have (reject outright; no fallback without authority):**
1. Reject the Seller's characterisation of positions as "FINAL," "settled" or "market standard." Ask for written evidence of any principal-level agreement.
2. Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance.
3. Title, capacity and fundamental warranties in a separate regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
4. Delete the blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion (8.3).
5. Replace general and deemed disclosure with specific fair disclosure only.
6. Bluefen: effective consent and evidence of conditions as a pre-Completion condition precedent.
7. Riverlark: payout and releases at Completion from Completion funds.

**Economics (hold our playbook positions):**
8. General cap: 25% / AUD 6m.
9. De minimis: AUD 5,000. Basket: AUD 50,000, first-dollar once exceeded.
10. General claims period: 24 months.
11. Bonuses: itemised or seller-funded, with on-costs quantified.

**Specific risk items:**
12. Ironquay: broaden the indemnity, keep the SOW3 cure, and obtain payment or assignment evidence.
13. Incident: preserve logs, investigate, require updates, and consider a specific indemnity without assuming any figure.
14. Sandbar: request contracts and assess; no automatic Debt or price deduction.
15. Tax and IP: keep open; reject "settled under the general regime."
16. Title: require independent evidence beyond DD-012.

**Information requests:**
- Riverlark payout letter and security release documents.
- Bluefen consent and evidence of conditions in clause 11.3.
- Ironquay SOW3 payment records and confirmatory assignment.
- Incident investigation scope, logs, and any notification analysis.
- Sandbar contracts and renewal terms.
- Bonus agreements and payroll-tax/super calculations.
- Independent title and encumbrance searches.
- Lease and Mossvale consent analysis.
- Cross-referenced SPA draft matching the summary clause numbers.

**Process:** Do not present the 20%/AUD 4.8m cap or the 18-month period as offers. Both need Amelia Frost's written approval identifying the specific draft, and neither has been given. Counsel should also confirm NSW enforceability of the fraud carve-out and of the exclusive-remedy and non-reliance wording.
=== END ADVICE ===
